title: Limerick loses out on a 28-acre Keen Road parcel it hoped to preserve
summary: Supervisors were set to vote on buying the light-industrial tract at 1 Keen Road, a target in the township's open space plan, but learned the owners had taken a competing offer. The board pre-authorized a $2.2 million purchase through Dec. 31 in case the other deal falls through.

title: Pottstown library warns of a funding crisis as budget season opens
summary: The Pottstown Regional Public Library has raised enough to start fixing its elevator but says it cannot keep operating without larger contributions from the borough and the three Pottsgrove townships. Losing passport services earlier this year cut about $100,000 from its $900,000 budget.

title: Phantoms football strings together a second straight win; volleyball outlasts Kennett
summary: Phoenixville's football team picked up its second consecutive victory on Friday night, and the girls volleyball team went five sets to beat Kennett and move to 10-8. Both programs turn to Pottstown next week.

title: Phoenixville-raised Olympic rower takes over Penn women's rowing
summary: Tyler Nase, who grew up along the Schuylkill in Phoenixville and rowed for the U.S. at the 2016 Rio Games, is the new head coach of the University of Pennsylvania women's rowing program. He returns to Penn, where his coaching career began, after leading Cornell's lightweight men.

title: Data center plan for the old Coventry Mall is withdrawn
summary: The developers behind an 85,987-square-foot data center proposed inside vacant space at The Shoppes at Coventry have pulled the application. North Coventry has cancelled the Oct. 22 zoning hearing that was to decide whether the use could go there.
loc: The Shoppes at Coventry, North Coventry

title: Pottstown council votes Oct. 13 on twin homes for the burned-out church lot
summary: A developer wants to build three pairs of twin homes where Transfiguration Lutheran Church stood until a fire destroyed it nearly a year ago. Council members gave the renderings a cool reception at Wednesday's work session, with the look of the brick facades a sticking point.

title: Whole Foods, L.L. Bean and Barnes & Noble headed to Upper Providence's District at Black Rock
summary: A 148,000-square-foot retail center on the former Quest Diagnostics campus off South Collegeville Road is about 89% pre-leased as construction starts, with Toll Brothers adding 122 townhomes next door. Completion is targeted for late 2027.
loc: 1201 S. Collegeville Rd, Upper Providence (near Oaks)

title: Google deal will add 348 megawatts at the Limerick nuclear plant
summary: Constellation's 20-year power-purchase agreement with Google funds turbine and control-system upgrades that raise the Limerick Clean Energy Center's output by 348 megawatts between 2028 and 2032. A union estimate puts the construction work at more than 2,500 local jobs.

title: Borough Council to vote Oct. 13 on reshuffling two downtown parking lots
summary: A proposed ordinance would renumber the Wheatland Street lot as Lot 12, designate a Bridge Street lot as Lot 6, let Municipal Building permit holders use Lot 6, and move the Babe Ruth League's seasonal parking to Lot 12.

title: Cleanup plan for the Nutt Road redevelopment site is open for public review
summary: Three Six Properties has filed a remedial investigation report and cleanup plan for 472 and 478 Nutt Road under the state's brownfield program. The documents can be reviewed at Borough Hall through Oct. 30.
